message.content:
**rs7412 (APOE) – allele frequency in European populations**

| Source | Population | Minor allele (C) frequency |
|--------|------------|---------------------------|
| 1000 Genomes Project (Phase 3) | EUR (combined European sub‑populations) | **≈ 0.15–0.18** |
| gnomAD v2.1.1 | Non‑Finnish European (NFE) | **≈ 0.16** |
| gnomAD v3.1.1 | European (EUR) | **≈ 0.17** |

> **Interpretation**  
> The C allele at rs7412 is the “ε2” allele of APOE. In most European cohorts it occurs in roughly 15–18 % of chromosomes (≈ 30–36 % of individuals are heterozygous, and ≈ 2–4 % are homozygous for the C allele).  

> **Variation across sub‑populations**  
> - Northern Europeans (e.g., Finnish, Swedish) tend to have slightly higher frequencies (~0.18–0.20).  
> - Southern Europeans (e.g., Italian, Spanish) show slightly lower frequencies (~0.13–0.15).  
> - The allele is much rarer in East Asian and African populations (MAF < 0.05).

These figures come from large, publicly available datasets (1000 Genomes, gnomAD) and represent the most up‑to‑date estimates as of 2024. If you need a precise number for a specific country or study cohort, let me know and I can look up the most recent data.
